data_quality_notes: Research phase completed inside its budget (finished 06:48 ET against a 07:24 cap) and logged a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so this report is not truncated. Five recommendations, not the 6-8 target, and zero intraday ideas — both deliberate. IDEA COUNT: research captured 14 candidates across 8 unique symbols; three were demoted to watchlist on their own evidence (TGT on an expected move larger than its stop, BTC on the correlation cap, IBB on having no dated catalyst) rather than published as filler. ZERO INTRADAY: this is a Saturday run. US equities and futures are closed, so every equity entry above is for the Monday 2026-08-17 open or later. The two asset classes that ARE live on a weekend both produced nothing publishable — ETH and SOL are sitting on braided moving averages with no trend to join, BTC is countertrend, and the event-contract feed is dead. PRICES: all five last_price values are Friday 2026-08-14 16:00 ET closes fetched from Finnhub, re-verified at synthesis. No price in this report is estimated. SOURCE FAILURES: no index, VIX, DXY, gold-futures or crude-futures quotes were obtainable — Yahoo returned HTTP 429, Finnhub index CFDs are paywalled, stooq 404'd on caret symbols and there is no AlphaVantage key; ETF proxies (SPY/QQQ/IWM/GLD/USO/UUP) were substituted throughout and the index levels in market_context.levels come from dated news reporting, not a live feed. NO EVENT CONTRACTS: the Kalshi feed via market_data.py returns only sports parlay shards for every macro query, so no market-implied probability could be read and no probability disagreement could be stated. This is a real loss on a weekend run, when event contracts are meant to carry more of the report. NO FUTURES: MES/MNQ/MCL/MBT are confirmed Robinhood-available via secondary sources, but robinhood.com's own futures-contract page returned HTTP 404, so no leveraged candidate was published on secondary sourcing alone. CONCENTRATION WARNING — read before sizing: all five ideas are long. There is no short and no hedge, three days after the S&P 500 set a record close of 7,798.99 and the Russell 2000 a record 3,067. A research pass specifically looking for a short found only downtrends that either report inside the window (BIDU, TJX, WMT) or ARE the steepener in disguise (TLT, at its 120-day low), so none was published. Separately, four of the five resolve materially on Wednesday 8/19: KRE, GLD and IWM on the 14:00 ET FOMC minutes — exactly at the correlation cap of three — and XLE on the 10:30 ET EIA report. KRE and IWM are close to the same domestic-steepener trade; treat their combined 5% as one position. Practically, this book is roughly three independent bets, not five. CONVICTION: nothing above 4. With the event feed dead, index/VIX/DXY quotes failing and crypto history rate-limited, this run has less confirming evidence than a clean one, and conviction is evidence quality rather than expected return. One research-log caveat: heading timestamps in notes.md drift 4-6 minutes ahead of the true clock and the log says so itself; all prices, levels and dates under those headings are fetched values.

market_context.summary: Record-high US indices with breadth broadening into the parts of the market that had lagged. The S&P 500 set a record close of 7,798.99 on 8/13 and the Russell 2000 a record 3,067, +23% YTD. Friday's tape was a clean reflation rotation: IWM +0.52%, XLE +1.39%, GLD +0.63%, SLV +0.55% against SPY -0.20%, QQQ -0.14%, TLT -0.67% and UUP -0.25% — money leaving duration and mega-cap growth for commodities and domestic small caps, with the 10y-2y steepening from +0.48 to +0.51. Macro supports it: July PPI came in unchanged versus +0.1% consensus, unemployment ticked down to 4.1%, and a 4.63% 10y against a 3.63% effective funds rate says the market is not pricing deep cuts. The tension is that a live US-Iran war is setting a floor under crude (Brent $87.07, WTI $81.25) — the same energy bid that supports XLE is the most plausible route to re-igniting inflation and ending the steepener. Cross-asset the picture is not uniformly risk-on: crypto is in a drawdown regime with BTC below its 20/50/100-day averages, and gold is only recovering from a six-month crash that took it 26% off its January peak. The week's hinge is Wednesday 8/19 — FOMC minutes at 14:00 ET, EIA at 10:30 ET, and TGT, LOW and TJX reporting before the open.

catalyst.event: FOMC minutes from the July 28-29 meeting, 14:00 ET; the curve reaction is the trade
catalyst.action: build the position before the 8/19 release; add on a dovish steepening reaction, cut on a hawkish flattening. Exit immediately on any single-name CRE credit event in the sector regardless of level.

recommendations.thesis: The 10y-2y spread widened to +0.51 on 8/14 from +0.48, with the 2y at 4.15% against a 3.63% effective funds rate — a bull steepener, which mechanically widens regional-bank net interest margin because these banks fund short and lend long. Sector reporting independently corroborates both the level and the mechanism: a 2s/10s spread of +0.52% and NIMs widening as deposit costs roll over, with KRE up 28% year on year. KRE closed 77.93, only 0.54% below its 120-day high of 78.35, with SMA20 76.48 and SMA50 74.81 stacked rising beneath it, so the balance sheet and the tape agree.
recommendations.key_risk: Commercial real estate credit is the sector-specific tail and it arrives without warning at the single-name level — the October 2025 loan problems at Zions and Western Alliance repriced the whole group in days. A CRE credit event does not care about the yield curve and bypasses the entire NIM thesis.
recommendations.counter_argument: One day of spread widening (0.48 to 0.51) is inside the noise band for the 10y-2y, and KRE is buying at the top of a 120-day range rather than at support, so the entry is close to the worst price in three months if the steepener is a head-fake. KRE also fell roughly 3% over a recent 30-day stretch on exactly the opposite narrative — that persistently high rates pressure NIM — which shows the sector will trade both readings of the same rate backdrop.

recommendations.thesis: GLD and SLV both bottomed on the same session, 2026-07-16, at 364.96 and 50.39 — a joint capitulation low across two separately traded metals is far harder to dismiss as single-instrument flow than either chart alone. GLD has since recovered to 401.48 and now sits above a rising SMA20 of 383.06 and SMA50 of 381.30. GDX confirms: at 89.97 it is 11.9% above its own SMA20 versus GLD's 4.8%, and miners leading bullion is the tell that the July low is being bought by people expressing a view rather than drifting.
recommendations.key_risk: This is a countertrend recovery inside a larger downtrend: GLD is still 19% below its 2026-01-29 peak of 495.90, and the 423-427 shelf that sets the first target is exactly where the January and May supply sits.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this is a bear-market rally in an asset that has fallen for six straight months, and that a joint bottom is just two correlated metals doing the same correlated thing. It also shares its rate-path direction with the KRE and IWM ideas — a hawkish 8/19 hurts all three together, so gold here is a hedge against equity risk-off but NOT against the rate-path bet this book is already making.

recommendations.thesis: Energy was the strongest sector into the weekend — XLE +1.39% and USO +1.26% on 8/14 — and it rallied the day AFTER Brent and WTI each fell more than 2% on 8/13 to $87.07 and $81.25, meaning equity buyers stepped in against a lower crude tape. XLE closed 61.91 with SMA20 59.16 above SMA50 56.97 and price 2.44% under its 120-day high of 63.46. Trump has declared the Iran ceasefire over and called negotiation a waste of time, which removes the near-term path to a supply-premium unwind.
recommendations.key_risk: Sized at 1% because the stop cannot be trusted. On 2026-04-08 a US-Iran ceasefire agreement crashed global crude by up to 20% in a single session — a dated precedent in this exact conflict this year, not a hypothetical. A repeat gaps XLE straight through the 57.80 stop, which is only 4.9% below entry, with no opportunity to exit at it.
recommendations.counter_argument: Crude fell 2% on 8/13 specifically on falling demand, not supply — if the demand signal is the real one, the war premium is the only thing holding energy up, and premiums decay. A sector whose bull case requires a war to continue has a short and unpleasant tail, and the April 8 session is proof of how fast that tail arrives.
